newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUBA'S KOEBNICK - FALL DMK NEED NOT HAVE IMPACT CPI.
newsitem.headline: BUBA'S KOEBNICK - FALL DMK NEED NOT HAVE IMPACT CPI.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said on Wednesday that the weakness of the German mark against the dollar this year was a normalisation of foreign exchange moves that was now complete.
He said the German's currency's fall need not have an impact on consumer prices, and added that there was no need to expect a continuation of the weakness.

"Of course the exchange rate development must be closely watched. No central bank can be interested in a currency suffering a sustained depreciation and possibly also high volatility," Koebnick told reporters at a news conference.
"Therefore it would surely not have been good if the mark depreciation against the dollar, which we have seen since the beginning of the year, had continued".
"But I think one need not have this fear. The development in recent weeks has shown that the dollar appreciation is not a one-way street," he added.
The Bundesbank official also said he would have no objection to the dollar at 1.70 marks.
"At present there would be little reason to object to a calm dollar development in the area of 1.70 marks in the foreseeable future," he said.

Koebnick also said that there were no strong reasons for greater volatility among European currencies although one could not rule out that speculation on EMU membership could influence the currency of a potential EMU nation.
